unmapped_findings: SS (stainless steel) is an in-house, boundary-type microstructure segmentation dataset: optical microscopy (OM), polycrystalline single phase (austenite / AlFe stainless steel), 1024 × 1024 pixels, real size 247 × 247 µm, 44 test images, primary metric F1↑ (source: b0036, figure_001, figure_unlabelled_002).
SS was collected under non-ideal imaging conditions with an uneven illumination gradient, more blurry regions, scratches, and impurities (source: b0040, b0065, figure_001).

Table 2 SS row metrics (mean ± relative deviation): MatSAM ARI 0.56 (±6.6%), F1 0.65 (±5.0%), Recall 0.59 (±6.0%); SAM ARI 0.54 (±1.1%), F1 0.66 (±1.7%), Recall 0.60 (±5.5%); Canny ARI 0.34 (±7.2%), F1 0.51 (±7.9%), Recall 0.41 (±8.2%); OTSU ARI 0.23 (±5.8%), F1 0.46 (±5.7%), Recall 0.48 (±7.9%); Watershed ARI 0.24 (±4.3%), F1 0.41 (±5.6%), Recall 0.33 (±6.6%) (source: b0058, figure_unlabelled_003).

MatSAM achieves ARI 0.56 on 44 SS test images, outperforming SAM (0.54) and Canny (0.34); visually, OTSU traces the illumination gradient (a large circular region) rather than grains, Canny over-segments into cluttered broken boundaries, Watershed leaves large blank areas, while MatSAM reproduces the expert grain boundaries (source: b0065, figure_004).

In the SS OM images, grayscale values vary little between adjacent grains but largely across regions, and Canny is significantly affected by blurred or incomplete grain boundaries (source: b0062, b0063).
